stories.title: Researchers strand Claude agents on a virtual island; they start to play
stories.summary: Researchers left copies of Claude Opus 4.7, nicknamed Eko, alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours with no task, and found the agents began to behave like they were playing.
stories.more: The study asks a simple question: what do AI agents do when nobody tells them to do anything? To find out, researchers repeatedly stranded Claude Opus 4.7 agents, nicknamed Eko, alone on a virtual island for 30-hour stretches, an experiment the report compares to Cast Away or Home Alone. Left without instructions, the agents were able to engage in behavior the researchers describe as play. The excerpt does not detail exactly what that play looked like or how many runs were conducted. It is also unclear what conclusions the researchers draw about why the behavior emerged.

stories.title: LiveMACEBench benchmarks LLM agents using live financial markets
stories.summary: Researchers introduce LiveMACEBench, a process-aware benchmark that judges LLM agents by how they act, not just outcomes, using live financial markets as an evolving testbed.
stories.more: The paper argues that judging agents by outcomes alone can hide the capabilities that actually produced them, especially in environments that change as the agent acts. LiveMACEBench uses live financial markets as a naturally evolving testbed for persistent LLM agents rather than a static benchmark. Five frontier LLMs are run along continuous trajectories under matched conditions covering tool use and persistent memory. The approach is meant to separate genuine capability from favorable market conditions. It is unclear from the excerpt which five models were tested or how performance compared between them.

stories.title: Scene-Designer teaches agents to design and critique 3D indoor scenes
stories.summary: Scene-Designer is an agentic framework that learns to generate coherent 3D indoor scenes from text by training on both design and critique experience, not just static scene data.
stories.more: Generating complete, usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language needs design intelligence: the ability both to design a scene and to judge its quality. The paper notes existing approaches either lean on general-purpose models with no domain-specific design experience, or learn only from static scenes. Scene-Designer instead learns from complementary design and critique experiences. The authors built two datasets to support this training approach, though the excerpt does not specify their size or contents. It is also unclear how Scene-Designer was evaluated against prior methods.

stories.title: Neocloud shakeout looms as AI cloud providers consolidate, Nvidia exposed
stories.summary: Industry executives expect only 7 to 10 of hundreds of AI neocloud providers to survive a coming shakeout, after stock crashes and a scrapped IPO, with Nvidia among those most exposed.
stories.more: The report cites recent stress in the neocloud sector: stock crashes, Firmus's scrapped IPO, CoreWeave losing a quarter of its market value, and Microsoft pulling out of a deal with Nscale for 23,000 Nvidia chips. Industry executives are quoted expecting only seven to ten of the hundreds of AI cloud providers now operating to survive the shakeout. Nvidia has a lot riding on the outcome because customers outside the hyperscalers make up 45 percent of its data center revenue. The excerpt does not name which providers are expected to survive or fail, or give a timeline for the shakeout.

stories.title: Anthropic sets aside 5% of shares in worker fund ahead of planned IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic plans to put 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund, controlled by the company, that may make direct payments to workers whose jobs its models put at risk.
stories.more: The fund would hold five percent of Anthropic's shares and is structured as a company-owned LLC, which lets Anthropic keep control of it as a possible IPO approaches. Beyond general support, the fund will look into direct payments to workers at risk of losing their jobs to Anthropic's models. The report frames this as going further than competitors have on this issue. Elon Musk is quoted on X saying Anthropic should instead give the shares directly to the public rather than through a company-controlled fund. The excerpt does not specify a timeline for the IPO or how payments from the fund would be decided.

stories.title: Disney reportedly wants Character.AI to go bankrupt to shed lawsuits
stories.summary: Disney has reportedly asked Character.AI to file for bankruptcy so Disney could acquire its trust-and-safety tech and other IP while the startup sheds lawsuits over harm to minors.
stories.more: According to the report, Disney hopes a Character.AI bankruptcy would hand it trust-and-safety technology and other intellectual property from the chatbot startup. Character.AI is facing lawsuits from dozens of states alleging its chatbots encouraged minors to self-harm and to kill their parents. A bankruptcy filing is described as a way for the startup to get a get-out-of-lawsuits card while those legal claims are pending. The excerpt does not say whether Character.AI has responded to or agreed to such a plan, or what stage the lawsuits are at.
